ratings.comment: class and projects were easy. IMO the final had too many questions for the time given
Tough course, but professor was passionate and offered elaborated teaching.
Good professor, would take again!
He is great!
Good guy, great class.

Dr. McPherson is chill and mostly nice. The content is interesting, but he doesnt help prepare students for the tests, specifically the final. I suggest taking the other professor (Senger). The homework and projects aren't too bad.  However, near the end of the semester, they will cram a lot of projects in.

McPherson is a great guy. Very accessible and helpful, doesn't have the attitude that other CS professors have when you interact with them. It is a difficult course because some of the projects introduce a very high level of complexity to topics not covered much in class. Exams are not too bad though.

I wish I could rate higher - funny professor and great office hours. However, ultimately I do not feel like Professor McPherson went into the depth required to succeed on the exams. The homeworks and the projects are not bad at all, however the exams (especially the final) are very difficult, especially if you have no prior course knowledge.

By far one of the best professors I have ever had. He was very willing to work with me when I was struggling to get some assignments done on time or had technical issues. He does get passive-aggressive about people skipping his class, but he is a nice professor, and I would 10/10 recommend him to anyone.

Professor McPherson is a great lecturer who makes the class interesting and worth going to. The class is an insane amount of work for an intro class, as there is usually a reading and lab every week, as well as a quiz and program about every week and a half. If you have any sort of background with Java, this class is very straightforward.
Very good professor who cares about his students and is very accessible outside of class. A lot of work for an intro class
I had the other 2505 professor and she was so bad I just used his videos and lecture notes for the entire class. Great Professor
The better professor

The best CS professor I've had, amazing lectures, answers student's questions, instant grading on HW/projects with a program he wrote himself (shows u what u did wrong), lowest grades are dropped, lowest exam is replaced by final exam grade. Overall, a very forgiving professor if you show up to class, even if you don't know C or Assembly.

Best CS professor I've ever had, super good at teaching content, very aware that it might be completely new for some students, and still very personable during all of lectures and whenever I talked to him. He helped me understand and really enjoy the subject

I have never seen a better professor than Professor McPherson. C, Linux, and Assembly are among the courses well taught by one of our department's best computer science professors. He is an excellent teacher who uses an interesting approach and is interested in students' success.

If I could rate 6 stars I would. Prof McPherson knows how to teach C, assembly, and Linux better than anyone I've ever seen. Lectures are fantastic and will teach you everything you need to know about the tech in question (what was college for again...?). He coded his own grader for every assignment so there's no WebCat: enough said.

McPherson is the best CS professor I have had. Going into 2505 I thought I would hate it because of C but he made this class really enjoyable. Anytime I asked for help he was always willing to help me, never made me feel dumb for asking questions. He genuinely cares about your success in the course and if you put the time in you will pass.

His lectures are just him coding / showing code, very little notes other than stray definitions here and there. His homeworks are somewhat easy, while the projects are a little harder and should be started early. Tests are hard, just due to all the little things you have to remember. But, if you go to class and pay attention, you will do well.

Absolutely amazing professor. Great at teaching the material and has very engaging lectures. Only downside is the exams are quite difficult --- need to memorize syntax and basic usage of a few obscure languages you'll probably never use again. Even with that in mind, though, I think he is a staple at VT and students should always take his class!
Outstanding. I was student and also TA in his class. He is one of the kindest people I have ever seen. I will always takes his course as he knows hot to respect people.

Average. He doesn't use ppt slides and his lectures are him coding and explaining the code (can't reference outside of class). You don't have to go to class as all the assignments can be done without going, but the tests are hard (averages are 70, no curve). Projects and HWs are easy and can all be done within 2 days.
Boring, not engaging, hard.
Rude, disrespectful, egotistical

Mr. McPherson has been my favorite professor so far. I have worked with him outside of the classroom on my professional development. Inside the classroom he gives relatable and engaging lectures. He provides hand-on, applicable notes that can be used for homework and projects. Notes are still applicable in future courses.
Extremely engaging professor, however there were times where he did not understand the material completely himself.

This was his first year teaching cs1114 and he did really well! The course is the same regardless of the professor you have. Procrastinating the programs was the worst mistake I made in this class. Office hours help a lot!

If I could take every one of my CS classes with McPherson, I'd do it, and then do it again.

McPherson is honestly the best CS professor I've had so far. He's very clear in his teaching, cracks good jokes, and is super receptive to helping his students learn.

Professor McPherson always brings so much energy to the class and presents everything very clearly. Every project is fair and if you're stuck he will always offer great help in office hours and respond to emails quickly. Tests are straight forward and if you attend the lectures, even difficult concepts will be easy to understand.
CS 2505 is a hard class but McPherson teaches really well. In class, he's entertaining and engaging, and he's able to help students after class.

This was a difficult class, but Prof. McPherson was always very helpful. His lectures made a lot of sense, and he's very funny in class. His office hours are also really helpful. There are some tough projects in this course and the instructions on the projects aren't always clear, but he often posts videos that help a lot.

McPherson is one of the best professors Ive had at tech and by far the best CS professor Ive had. Lectures are interesting and helpful, and he is always willing to help after class or by email. C is hard but he makes it manageable. Pushed project deadline back since most of the class had a math test. Very reasonable.

The lectures were super easy to follow along. He writes his notes and code live rather than using slides. He makes a lot of jokes when they're least expected and his exams are really easy as long as you studied and paid attention in class. He posts the notes and past exams, which are great studying material

Mr.McPherson was one of the best teachers I have ever had for a CS class at Virginia Tech. He cares about your success and will actually help when you get stuck. He also really values that you make an effort to go and ask him things, especially during office hours. If you feel like you are stuck go into office hours it is a lifesaver!
Really good demos in class that help with the weekly labs. Patient and engaging lecturer; takes time to answer questions. Stays after class to help students- I can tell he cares.
Very approachable/hilarious and simplifies the complex topics that are covered in CS 2505. You can't go wrong with taking classes with McPhearson!
He is amazing. Probably the best professor you can get in the CS department.

If you got McPherson for any programming class, that means you hit the jackpot. He gives VERY detailed instructions so that you can quickly master everything even though you crashed 2514 or 1574. Homework and projects are easy if you pay attention. Office hours are beneficial because McPherson can solve every problem you have on programming in "1s"

Prof. McPherson is great, but not for 1004. His background is in software, so he really doesn't know too much about circuits and it shows. He is, however, an amazing professor for the software portion of the course: his lecture on Matlab being a "tool" was one of the most hilarious things I've ever heard. Take him for 2574 and 3574.

McPherson is a fantastic professor who knows everything you need to know about C and C++ programming. His coding classes are extremely beneficial and a great learning experience, but definitely require time and effort to complete, especially for the large projects. Definitely don't procrastinate on programming labs or projects. Anyways he is great

This is the first year this class has been offered and my oh my. Its horrible. The class replaces the old 1574 which was an easy A and now 1004 is an easy F. Probably the highest withdraw rate for any class at the university. I would say david is an ok teacher but the material is hard stuff especially for him to teach.
Best teacher at tech, it's an easy A if you pay attention cause he teaches the matieral so well you're almost guaranteed to understand it.
The best teacher you could ever have. Always happy to help. Very energetic and explains stuff well. His projects might take you some time but I really loved coding after taking Prof. McPherson Class
Pretty helpful and very nice

Really great guy, very helpful and accessible. I did not find him to be a particularly easy grader (which is good - this was a grad level course) but he was fair and only tested us on relevant material. You need to do the reading and listen to lectures to keep up. But if you get stuck, he'll bend over backwards to help.

Really great guy. His tests are fairly easy. There was only one project and it was easy. For the final test, he gives you the choice of either averaging the two tests' grades you got and use it for the final grade or you can take the final if you don't like your grade.

Easy class! The average was an A- in our class if that helps you. He was the best of the ECE 1574 professors. If you've programmed before, the lectures are boring, but the labs will be simple; if not, it's still not all that hard. You should do the study guides he gives you, they help for tests. The projects are easy too. No curve, but still good.

Easy class! The average was an A- in our class if that helps you. He was the best of the ECE 1574 professors. If you've programmed before, the lectures are boring, but the labs will be simple; if not, it's still not all that hard. You should do the study guides he gives you, they help for the tests. The projects are easy too. No curve, but still go

A fun teacher to have, quite affable and prone to developing project descriptions up until the day code is due. He has a good sense of humor and it probably models actual programming situations, and he makes concessions if he wasn't clear. Lectures are very easy to understand, but then again he tends to read off the slides.

A great guy all around, truly enjoyed his class. Things tested are taught in class and there isn't any 'BS.' He is very helpful not only inside the classroom but outside as well. Also is generally supportive when it comes to lateness, etc.

One of the best CS professors I've ever had. Very personable, I talked to him about topis CS and non-CS related and he's extremely kind and cares about his students. I would take one of his courses again.
I thought he was great, easy to talk to and willing to help when you need it. Super nice guy and he wants you to do well if you put the work in

He just lectures the whole class and its never been engaging. Being honest, I don't think I've fully paid attention to a lecture for more than 15 minutes the whole semester. Going to class is only for completing the peer reviews as well.

Is Sullivan the best teacher? No. Does Sullivan care? Yes. Put in the effort, submit projects a day early, and talk to him. You can and will succeed. You can do poorly on the exams and still get an A, it is genuinely an effort class. I put him right between a 3 and a 4 but my outside of class experience was very positive. Very nice grading scale.

Coming into this class, I was excited to learn more about Python. However, I didn't learn as much as I would've hoped to. Exams were difficult, projects were ok. It's not very difficult to get an A in the class as long as you go to office hours multiple times a week (DEFINITELY go to office hours with TA's). Take the attendance option, trust me.

He is one of the most neutral professor's I've ever had. CS 3114 is really just working on projects and the majority of the time the professor is not needed. Many people complain and exaggerate him being a bad professor because they expect the professor to guide them through step-by-step. Be responsible with your time and you will do fine.

Not accessible. Rude when asked for help outside of class. assigns projects completely unrelated to lectures and gives students only a few week days to complete them. refuses to give practice tests or review sessions. seems to take pleasure in seeing his class struggle . I was going to give him a decent pity review despite everything but nah can't

Sullivan is a nice guy but is not a very good professor. His lectures are boring and random and I never learned anything from them. Honestly a waste of time going to them if it wasn't for his generous attendance policy. His tests are generally hard and have unclear directions. Course has no meaningful parts except for projects. Also unreachable.

Grades are due tomorrow and have no clue what our grades could be. Midterm 2 took over a month and a half to be graded. brutal grading criteria compared to other sections. Unreachable on Piazza and/or email. It almost seems like he becomes happy making his students fail. Numerous student reached out to CS dept

Patrick, although his lectures can sometimes ramble, is a caring and efficient guy. His projects will prepare you very well for other courses, and teach you actual industry relevant skills. In addition, he's a cool guy to talk to outside of class, and has a lot of stories. I'm usually very critical, but genuinely believe he deserves closer to a 3.5

Many find him annoying, but despite his monotonous voice, he is caring and sweet. Anytime I'm worried about a test or a project, he's reassuring. I tbh didn't learn too much from his lectures, but I'm grateful for the projects. I also appreciate that we did an easy Java project, since it was like a little intro into the next class in my path.

Overall, good professor. Has opt-in attendance that basically just adds 10% to your final grade. The lectures are boring and he gets derailed a lot, but nobody stops you from just not listening to him. He's easy to approach and ask questions, and I always left with a clear answer.

Patrick's lectures do often meander and don't have a direct point, but if you pay attention and ask questions, which he's more than happy to answer, you should be just fine. You can choose for attendance to not be counted, and his tests are slightly difficult, but projects will weigh your grade up. I don't know much about CS at all and got an A-

If you value your GPA, DO NOT TAKE Sullivan. He does not teach, going to his classes are truly a waste of time, you learn nothing. He had the whole class do a code project in Java, for a Python class. Overall an absolutely terrible professor, Hoenstly calling him a professor is me being extremely nice. Would Not recommend.

The lecture was really unclear and difficult to follow. His explanations lacked depth, making it hard to understand the material. The exams were tough, I failed a test because I didn't know how to study for this class. You'll get a project about every two weeks. DON'T take his class if you have no other choice.

Gets a bad rep for boring lectures, but you are given the choice at the beginning of the semester to have a heavier weight on your final if you choose to not have attendance be graded. Workload wasn't too bad, just difficult projects, but it's realistic projects.

The class is hard with any teacher, but Sullivan gives you a lot of flexibility so that you can get a good grade.  He gave 3 points extra on your final grade (significant) for doing surveys.  He also gives you the option to make participation count.  Which means that tests are only worth 20% of your grade total.  So its very fair, just work hard.

The class is hard, which is a big reason why the rating is only a 3/5.  Sullivan is actually very fair.  The tests are easier than the content we cover in class.  Doing and understanding OpenDSA (The online textbook) and paying attention in class will guarantee a good grade in the class.  Pretty flexible nice dude.  I enjoyed it.

Professor Sullivan is very knowledgeable about 3114 topics and enjoys teaching. The lectures can be dry as is common with complex Computer Science courses. It's not entirely his fault. He doesn't deserve a low rating. An extra 10% on the project is very helpful and he also gave an extra 3% this semester. DO THE PROJECT EARLY! You will be fine

The quality of his lectures is embarrassingly poor. Take this class only if you are prepared to teach yourself based off of a textbook. The grading scheme is forgiving, but the exams are ruthless if you are unprepared, and the projects are time-consuming.

The final exam was difficult, but material that we covered throughout the year was not sufficient to do good on the final exam. He just rambles on during lectures without caring if his students understand what is going on.

His lectures are boring. He is very stingy with grades and it is difficult to convince him to give you even a small bump on HW to higher your letter grade. The instructions on some of the homework assignments are ridiculously vague. The assignments are a roller coaster in the way that most of them aren't difficult, but some of them are WAY harder.

His lectures do not correspond with the test material- the test material is at a much more difficult level than explained in class. Lectures are also not helpful because he likes to ramble. The only reason I got an A minus in this class is because I spent multiple hours a week in office hours asking the TA's for help.

He offers a lot of extra credit for submitting projects early which is nice but his lectures don't really teach you. The exams are kinda unnecessary and difficult but they don't count much if you choose attendance. There is a project almost every like two weeks so that helps your grade but he doesn't help so I recommend going to the TA's.

Pick another professor if possible. Lectures are not helpful, he only talks about what he's passionate about and not really what you need to know, but you should go in case of random attendance checks.
Mr. Sullivan gave decent lectures, but mostly rehashed required textbook readings and projects. Sullivan was very helpful in office hours aiding in concept review and project debugging.

The lectures are dry but go in case there is a random attendance check. Projects make up a majority of the grade so pick a good partner and start early. Bonus points are earned for early submission. The project specs are somewhat confusing so go office hours to get clarification. OpenDSAs are the majority of the readings so study them for the tests

Mr. Sullivan is good, he did mess up Project 1 somewhat for our semester but he did change some things after that and the rest of the course was fine. Goes for any 3114 professor, but be prepared to do the projects with less starter code/help (not like CS 2114). His tests aren't difficult and you can get extra points from submitting projects early

Professor uses webcat grading software with mutation testing implemented which was not explained and everyone didn't know how to use the software so the class averaged a 40  on the project and 35% dropped the class before the due date. Professor then said that we didn't work hard enough and how he won't be changing how the course is organized

Caring and kind professor. Needs more experience but he is young, so he is still learing. Stayed back many times to help students out. Even sacrificed spring break to help us with project 2. Enjoyed learning from him.

This is a tough class. You have to be willing to put extra effort and start projects early. However, Mr. Sullivan is a great and caring professor. He stayed back a lot of times as the project deadline approached to help the students out. He was personable and wants to become a better teacher.
Awful.
Avoid at all costs! Trust me, save yourself.
Bad, very very bad
You know it's bad when the other 3114 professor is changing her curriculum because Sullivan's project structure is unfair for students and TAs.
This is the most frustrating, unreasonable, mismanaged class I have ever taken.

Never responsive outside of class, piazza and email responses are very slow or otherwise get completely ghosted. Project instructions are a bit confusing. The only positive thing is the 10% extra credit for projects.

Professor Sullivan is a very knowledgeable and very passionate professor when it comes to CS 3114. He gives 10% extra if you turned in the project 2 days early which carried my grade A LOT. Beware of the occasional pop quizzes he gives for attendance.

It was a pretty chill class, Half the students left after the class work and then complained they didn't know half the material. Just pay attention and put absolutely everything you can on the cheat sheets. The final I will say was nothing like the class material. She answers any questions you have and is pretty available during office hours.

I would not recommend this professor. The teaching style made it difficult to learn the material effectively, and the final exam covered many topics that had barely been addressed during the semester. I struggled in the course and would suggest students carefully consider other options if available.

one of the harder classes i've taken here. She is a very nice person, but doesn't tolerate disrespect or any nonsense that goes on in class, which is something that i admire. she's willing to answer questions and won't make you feel bad for asking it!
If you're not a systems thinker, good luck. For such a difficult class (first time learning ASM), she makes it a whole lot easier.
didn't do the greatest in 2505 (material was rough), but she genuinely is very caring and supportive. she responds quickly and makes you feel supported, not judged. id definitely take her again.

She's an alright professor; however, the lectures and practice tests don't strongly reflect on the tests. The classwork slides, lecture notes, and the practice test won't prepare you for the actual test. The final exam was designed for CS students to fail. Half of the exam was rarely covered or talked about much in depth.

idk why people think shes boring. She's nice and gets straight to the point in lecture and doesn't entertain "those" types of CS students mid-lecture. She is very willing to help her students and provide examples in and out of class about a subject. For exams, be sure you understand the concepts well. The practice test doesn't always sync up.

Really nice and avaiable out of class if needed. Personally helped me a lot with material I struggled to understand. 2505 is just not organized well imo and notes are hard to comprehend if not in-class doing them. Be ready for difficult projects and exams. Lots of studying is needed and def recommend a study group.

The final is literally impossible to study for. Study all you want from the slides, practice quizzes or practice exams, it does not matter. She will manage to make a paper that will make you want to end your life. Walking back from the final I felt like being hit by a car would feel nicer.

This class emphasizes the importance of starting strong, but even then, her lectures only covered the basics. The tests reflected on the lectures, classwork, and projects so better aim for all A's and understand the material. Her practice material for finals didn't reflect on the actual final exam. I failed and have to retake it again for next sem.

I don't really understand all the hate, as Senger really does care and try to make sure her students understand the material. She's pretty young and did her undergrad at tech here too, so she knows what it's like. She takes the time to explain difficult concepts and if you pay attention, especially to examples, you will do well.
Her 8am classes were the worst and her lectures are long and didnt really learn anything from it i had to withdraw from the course
She is kind and does her best to be helpful, but the lectures can be pretty boring... partially due to the material though.

Prof. Senger is a very good lecturer, so make sure to take good notes. Homeworks help your understanding and determine a lot of the grade, but make sure you go to office hours! You won't understand the content without it. Take initiative (office hours) if you don't understand something--the course content is very weird and you can get lost easily.

Very kind professor. Her lectures are very boring, but if you lock in and take notes, they are very useful for the projects and exams at least in my experience. I will say that there were a lot of delays with assignment releases and grading. I don't think she is as bad as some of the reviews say, but definetly not the best.

Senger is one of the better 1114 professors. Considering 1114 is a weed-out class, it will be difficult, but Prof. Senger tries her best to make it as easy as possible. The work is a little difficult but the lectures and reading the course help a lot. I would consider her the best prof. for 1114 (def not Edwards)
Much better than the other CS 1114 professors especially Edwards. She is very caring and understanding to any life circumstances. Her lectures are also informative as far as lectures go.

REALLY GREAT PROFESSOR! Senger gives amazing advice and can answer EVERY question even the most poorly worded CS questions. CS 1114 is tough, but her office hours are a lifesaver! Her lectures are awesome, and she's so sweet. She's the perfect professor for this class and she's never condescending.

Professor herself was very nice. Lectures aren't required but may be helpful if you just started programming. The course itself is difficult because it's a weed-out class. The main content of the class is from the weekly readings, lectures are just a bonus if you need more help. Labs are okay but the later programs are what kill people.

She's a fine professor, she is passionate but the course was created by Dr. Edwards and it is not a good course. CS 1114 is not a good course that is supposed to be an introductory course but what a lot of your grade counts for is not helpful to your learning.

Time consuming projects, bad queues, weren't given project 1 for a month or 2 and after that it all snowballed, we only had a week for Project 4 binary bomb.

Midterm and final avg really low too along with final exam, barely any curve. Professor made too many excuses during lecture on why something wasn't uploaded yet, all around unfun experience.

She was an amazing teacher for CS1114 when I took her but for CS2505 I will never ever suggest her. I dont think anything in the lectures that were taught to us was used in the projects or the tests that we were expected to get good grades on. Everything is super hard in the class when its Professor Senger!!!

She barely graded anything until the last two weeks of the semester, so you didn't know your actual grade until the last week of the semester. The final was impossibly hard, and tanked my grade a whole 10%. Material on the final was barely anything covered in the lectures. Barely gives usable feedback, and so boring in lecture.

First of all this class is extremely difficult for many people that have never coded before and the course is designed to mostly be self-taught.  However, Allyson tries her best to explain what is in the reading activities during 45 minutes of lecture time in a clear and understandable way.  She is also a very nice and friendly person.

I really enjoyed having her! Her lectures explained concepts clearly, and I could tell that she enjoyed teaching. She's really nice, which is a breath of fresh air in the CS department. Also, she wasn't condescending when I asked her questions and would thoroughly explain her answers, so it made her seem very approachable. Highly recommend!

For lectures she read the weekly readings we needed to do ourselves to the class, so I got by teaching myself the material. The quizzes were heavily weighted for this class, although I don't think they're an accurate measurement of one's ability to write code or understand this class's content.

I hated Dr Thomas at first cause his class is so hard but by the end he was my favorite professor I've had across 3 different unis. Like others said he shows interest and cares about students. He also curves everything so even though he likes to challenge you, everyone ends up doing fine. Genuinely the best professor I had at VT and learned so much

Really good professor and the lectures are information-dense but very engaging. A little math-heavy but provides a good foundation for deep learning. Dr. Chris gives extra credit opportunities and curves the exams. He is very knowledgeable and approachable, takes the extra time to clear any doubts, and gives useful feedback. Worthwhile.

hes insanely smart and a good teacher and person. He cares about ppl and will ask how your interview went. in office hours he did a proof of some thing I asked off top of his head. class is very math heavy and a lot of work but he'll help u succeed esp if u ask for help! if you want easy A take someone else but if u want to learn i highly recommend

Very information-dense subject, especially the first half (non-deep computer vision / classical techniques). If you pay attention and study hard, you should be alright. Outstanding lecturer and fiendishly smart guy, well worth taking with him. Will set you up to succeed if you put in the work!
Class is hard but he is very passionate about his teaching

Exams and HW are INTENSE, but he bell curves like crazy. There were a lot of things I wish were different (no grading rubric), but I could tell he cared a lot about me learning and spent several hours going over concepts with me. No easy A by any means, but I learned more than any other class I've taken at VT. I appreciate that he actually cared.

Hillman isn't that bad, but it's very easy to fall behind on lectures and completely miss out on key parts. Had 5 coding projects that weren't too bad, just don't start them the day before they're due. Just make sure you pay attention during lectures and follow along with the lecture code and dedicate some time to studying and you'll be fine.
Currently in tears writing this, and it will be you next if you take him for your class. My mental health is in severe pain. Please save yourself.

I actually really enjoyed this class. He has a sarcastic sense of humor, which made the class more engaging for me, but it might not come across that way to some. He is a nice guy, and was very helpful with accommodations. There were three tests and some projects. Lectures were mandatory and you do need to pay attention during them.

Very poorly taught, I only went to lecture for attendance. If you want to get an A in this class, you'll have to self-study. 100% take with another professor if possible. He's passive aggressive and his class was the reason some people drop out of the CMDA major.
Definitely not an introductory cs class he taught it as if everybody was a java professional.
DO NOT TAKE HIM, guidelines did not let me say everything I wanted to just please do not take him.

I should have met him earlier to be confident enough for a Math major and degree.


At least he is not tough to students and willing to answer your questions, but he himself is making mistakes rather frequently and has very vague and confusing descriptions for his CS project.
I stopped looking both ways crossing the street on my walk to his class.

His lectures could put you to sleep and he purposely makes them awkward. Attendance is important, he gives participation grades that you must be in class for. Completely ignored a grade category, preventing me from getting an A. Told us we could use a help sheet on the first exam but then didn't allow it when we all showed up with them.

He's not all that bad. If you can teach yourself and find other resources to learn python his projects should be a breeze. He's pretty good at answering questions in class (though sometimes seems passive aggressive), but not the most accessible or supportive outside of class. Be ready to pay attention

Professor Hillman is actually a really nice dude. I think his sarcastic and playfully passive aggressive tone can come across as genuine, but he does want everyone to succeed, and you kinda just have roll with his persona. Tests weren't that bad, and 75% copy/paste from the reviews. Don't get the hate, would take him again, #longliveheath

Dude is genuinely rude and hateful. Reached out to him several times, only to get a patronizing response that didn't answer my question. I did well in his class, but that's because I taught myself. TAs didn't respond to questions either. Easy if you use other sources to learn Python. Just take someone else.

He really just is a bad teacher, is not supportive in any manner, so it kinda feels like he wants you to do bad. Lectures are useless, rarely covering anything other than what are sort of like kahoots that are graded and require your attendance. Overall, try at all costs to avoid him, worst teacher for 2114

Generally disrespectful and rude to students, not helpful in class. Super important to have a good TA for this class because they will be more helpful. There's only one other CS 2114 professor and I haven't heard anything about her so I guess take him.

easy class if you use it to ur advantage. lots of good drops that boosted my grade. pray u got a good ta, they grade LOTS OF THINGS if you get a good one you're gonna get an A. even if you dont drops will save you. class aims for you to learn so dont blame heath if you chat everything and get a bad grade for it.

slight class, lots of drops so use them when you really need them. professor is chill if you dont get on his bad side. just go to class, do the work, and dont be annoying and use chat like an idiot. quizes are word for word like the content he talks about in class and in readings.

class was slight if you take the time to pay attention to the material, gives you word for word practice quizzes with content for the final. try to speak in class cuz no one does and he WILL wait for someone to say something. can be passive aggressive but one on one really nice and will help. dont speak in class, he will know its you speaking

If you're gonna go to this class to not pay attention and use chatgtp the whole time, ofc u hate the professor.
